newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA's TAT, Air Liberte seek to slash losses.
newsitem.headline: BA's TAT, Air Liberte seek to slash losses.

text.p: The chairman of TAT and Air Liberte, French units of British Airways, said in an interview that he sought wage cuts, particularly at TAT, to cut their losses to 300 million francs in 1997 from 1.2 billion last year.
Cockpit crew unions began a 48-hour strike today.

"We can't sustain the pilot and flight engineer costs, which are too high in France and notably with us," Marc Rochet told La Tribune. "Certainly we need to discuss how to lower costs, as is happening at Air France Europe. But negotiating under pressure is out of the question," he said. He said demands put forward by the staff would raise costs by 18 percent.
"We need to reduce the costs of pilots and flight engineers by around 15 percent at TAT," he said. He said he needed to add, in fairness, that they had accepted a 15 percent cut in 1996.
"In all, TAT needs to lower pilot and flight engineer costs by 30 percent, about what Air France is asking," he said.
He said Air Liberte's costs were lower. He added that it would not be reasonable on the staff's part to expect a 13th month's wage, as is customary in France.
Rochet reiterated his objective to bring TAT and Air Liberte to breakeven in two years. He said Air Liberte lost around one billion francs in 1996 and TAT lost 200 million.
"This year I hope to divide the loss by four, which would represent a loss of 300 million francs," he said. "If we don't succeed, the future of the two airlines would be seriously threatened."
